methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly naming AI data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide signals structural concentration risks—infrastructure investment flowing to metro areas while rural communities face displacement pressures without capability gains.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership creates institutional anchor for deep AI education in Richmond metro, but geography-specific model suggests replicability barriers that could reinforce hub-based concentration rather than distributed fluency.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches online workforce training program - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Online workforce training platform from Roanoke College enables distributed access to AI-adjacent skills outside traditional tech hubs, though depth and completion rates will determine whether this enables genuine peer-to-peer fluency or remains shallow adoption.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce indicates capability demands concentrating in metros where AI adoption accelerates faster than skills development—a depth/pace problem within urban centers rather than distribution challenge.

signals.title: Why Darden Is Moving AI Into the Core MBA Experience - Darden Report Online
signals.signal_reading: Darden integrating AI into core MBA curriculum signals elite institutions deepening capabilities among already-privileged cohorts, reinforcing credential-based concentration unless curriculum models diffuse to community colleges and regional universities.
